subject: Residency playbook: approval, governance and EU/APAC switchover kickoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Mina Tan <mina.tan@acmecloud.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency playbook: approval, governance and EU/APAC switchover kickoff

Hi all,

Thanks for moving quickly on the ACME private deployment. We're at the point where we need governance approval and a mutual action plan for EU/APAC residency + warm-standby failover. Attached is the residency playbook draft (residency_playbook_draft_v1.pdf) and a lightweight topology sketch.

High-level asks in this kickoff:
- ACME to confirm acceptable cutover windows and change-control lead for each region (APAC/EU).
- Agree on ownership for prefix announcements and DNS failover (Redwood ops vs ACME network team).
- Confirm KMS custody model for any EU-resident keys (bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed).
- Approve a canary and rollback plan for the first switchover exercise.

Please review the playbook and reply with: 1) A primary approver for legal/security; 2) Any mandatory audit evidence ACME requires ahead of the cutover (I attached acme_soc2_qna.xlsx as a starting list); 3) Network contact for peering/BGP talks.

Proposed timelines: internal signoff by 2025-07-06, canary on 2025-07-20, full readiness review 2025-07-27. If that doesn't work for ACME, propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0132

Attachments: residency_playbook_draft_v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB), network_topology_sketch.png (png, 120KB), acme_soc2_qna.xlsx (xls, 230KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Mina Tan <mina.tan@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency playbook: approval, governance and EU/APAC switchover kickoff

Jordan, Mina —

Quick technical notes from infra:
- For failover we should prefer regional-egress routing with per-region load balancing + BGP tie-break rather than cross-region NAT traversal. That keeps egress locality intact and reduces audit surface.
- We'll present two options for prefix ownership: (A) Redwood announces customer-specific prefixes from regional edges (Redwood-managed, quicker), or (B) ACME announces their own prefixes via a shared peering (ACME-managed, preferred by many regulated customers).
- KV cache ownership: during warm-standby the cache TTL and sync window will determine RTO. I recommend short TTLs on user-level KV and explicit cache-warmup steps in the canary.
- KMS: if ACME requires BYOK/HSM for EU keys we'll use a customer-keystore workflow (requires provisioning window and SAML/IAM mapping).

I've attached a rough network topology that shows BGP peering candidates and expected egress paths.

Marcus
Marcus Lin, Principal Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: network_topology_sketch.png (png, 120KB)

From: Mina Tan <mina.tan@acmecloud.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Legal <legal-agents@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 02:05:00 +09:00
Subject: Re: Residency playbook: approval, governance and EU/APAC switchover kickoff

Thanks Jordan and Marcus. A few points from ACME side:

1) Change window: APAC prefers weekends 02:00–06:00 JST; EU prefers 00:00–04:00 CEST on Sat/Sun. We need a documented rollback SLA (target 30 minutes) and a post-mortem within 24h.

2) Prefix ownership: ACME legal and network ops prefer option B (ACME announces prefixes). We'll need the peering contract and an IP ownership attestation.

3) KMS: ACME will insist on BYOK for EU-resident keys. Please send the technical steps and timeline for HSM provisioning.

4) Canary: we'll run a DNS-based canary for 48h routing 2% of traffic to Redwood warm-standby. We also require a read-only access token for Redwood's audit logs during the canary (7 days retention minimum).

I'll loop in our on-call network lead (cc'ed separately) to schedule the peering call. Legal will look at the SOW and return redlines.

Best,
Mina Tan
Head of Cloud Engineering, ACME Media
mina.tan@acmecloud.com

--
Mina Tan
ACME Media

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Mina Tan <mina.tan@acmecloud.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency playbook: approval, governance and EU/APAC switchover kickoff

Mina — thanks, that's helpful. Action items I'm capturing here:

1) ACME to confirm peering contact and provide IP attestation (owner: Mina) — target 2025-07-03.
2) Redwood (Marcus) to publish a BYOK/HSM provisioning doc and estimated lead time — target 2025-07-06.
3) Legal (ACME + Redwood legal) to exchange SOW redlines — target 2025-07-07.
4) Redwood infra to produce a short 'canary runbook' that includes DNS failover steps, metrics we will monitor, and rollback triggers — target 2025-07-10.

I'll prep a mutual action plan doc (link: https://redwood.app/drive/residency-playbook-v1) and will send a calendar invite for a 2025-07-08 governance call (30 minutes) to review final cutover windows.

Also: Priya, can you confirm procurement lead for ACME and whether we need a purchase order before SOW signature?

Thanks,
Jordan

Governance note: Redwood approves moving forward with the proposed schedule provided ACME signs the attestation for prefix ownership and agrees to the rollback SLA. For BYOK we will require a short integration window (approx 7 business days) to validate key rotation and access controls. Marcus — please include confirmation of the IAM mapping steps in your BYOK doc.

I'll join the governance call on 2025-07-08. If there are any last-minute security questions, loop in Soojin who will be our security reviewer.

Approved to proceed to canary planning pending the items above.

Best,
